arxiv-1809-05085.title: Work and Heat Value of Bound Entanglement
arxiv-1809-05085.creator: Aslı Tuncer, Mohsen Izadyari, Ceren B. Dağ, Fatih Ozaydin, Özgür E. Müstecaplıoğlu
arxiv-1809-05085.description: Abstract Entanglement has recently been recognized as an energy resource which can outperform classical resources if decoherence is relatively low. Multi-atom entangled states can mutate irreversibly to so called bound entangled (BE) states under noise. Resource value of BE states in information applications has been under critical study and a few cases where they can be useful have been identified.

arxiv-2012-03200.title: Pandemic Risk Management: Resources Contingency Planning and Allocation First version: April 8, 2020.
arxiv-2012-03200.creator: Xiaowei Chen, Wing Fung Chong, Runhuan Feng, Linfeng Zhang
arxiv-2012-03200.description: Abstract Repeated history of pandemics, such as SARS, H1N1, Ebola, Zika, and COVID-19, has shown that pandemic risk is inevitable. Extraordinary shortages of medical resources have been observed in many parts of the world. Some attributing factors include the lack of sufficient stockpiles and the lack of coordinated efforts to deploy existing resources to the location of greatest needs.

arxiv-2105-09980.title: Data-driven discovery of interpretable causal relations for deep learning material laws with uncertainty propagation
arxiv-2105-09980.creator: Xiao Sun Bahador Bahmani, Nikolaos N. Vlassis, WaiChing Sun, Yanxun Xu
arxiv-2105-09980.description: Abstract This paper presents a computational framework that generates ensemble predictive mechanics models with uncertainty quantification (UQ). We first develop a causal discovery algorithm to infer causal relations among time-history data measured during each representative volume element (RVE) simulation through a directed acyclic graph (DAG).

arxiv-2208-08938.title: Meta Sparse Principal Component Analysis
arxiv-2208-08938.creator: Imon Banerjee, Jean Honorio
arxiv-2208-08938.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Imon Banerjee, Jean Honorio. We study the meta-learning for support (i.e. the set of non-zero entries) recovery in high-dimensional Principal Component Analysis. We reduce the sufficient sample complexity in a novel task with the information that is learned from auxiliary tasks. We assume each task to be a different random Principal Component (PC) matrix with a possibly different support and that the support union of the PC matrices is small.

arxiv-2211-07137.title: DroneNet: Crowd Density Estimation using Self-ONNs for Drones
arxiv-2211-07137.creator: Muhammad Asif Khan, Hamid Menouar, Ridha Hamila
arxiv-2211-07137.description: Abstract Video surveillance using drones is both convenient and efficient due to the ease of deployment and unobstructed movement of drones in many scenarios. An interesting application of drone-based video surveillance is to estimate crowd density (both pedestrians and vehicles) in public places.

arxiv-2409-05501.title: On the model uncertainties for the predicted maximum depth of extensive air showers
arxiv-2409-05501.creator: Sergey Ostapchenko, Günter Sigl
arxiv-2409-05501.description:
A 2024 arXiv research paper by Sergey Ostapchenko, Günter Sigl. Abstract

A quantitative analysis of model uncertainties
for calculations of the maximum depth of proton-initiated extensive air showers (EAS) has been performed. Staying within the standard physics picture and using the conventional approach to the treatment of high energy interactions, we found that present uncertainties on the energy dependence of the inelastic cross section, the rate of diffraction, and the inelasticity of hadronic collisions allow one to increase the predicted
average EAS maximum depth by about 10 g/cm
2
.

arxiv-2409-11104.title: Depth-based Privileged Information for Boosting 3D Human Pose Estimation on RGB
arxiv-2409-11104.creator: Alessandro Simoni, Francesco Marchetti, Guido Borghi, Federico Becattini, Davide Davoli, Lorenzo Garattoni, Gianpiero Francesca, Lorenzo Seidenari, Roberto Vezzani
arxiv-2409-11104.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Alessandro Simoni, Francesco Marchetti, Guido Borghi, Federico Becattini, Davide Davoli, Lorenzo Garattoni, Gianpiero Francesca, Lorenzo Seidenari, Roberto Vezzani. Despite the recent advances in computer vision research, estimating the 3D human pose from single RGB images remains a challenging task, as multiple 3D poses can correspond to the same 2D projection on the image. In this context, depth data could help to disambiguate the 2D information by providing additional constraints about the distance between objects in the scene and the camera.

pmc-13116492.description: Highlights Public health relevance—How does this work relate to a public health issue?
